Thanks for the ping — technical note below.

Short answers:
- Retention: We never intentionally copy or store customer session tokens in third-party analytics subprocessors. The artifacts your transfer log shows look like transient request metadata and small KV cache entries used for short-lived routing heuristics. Those are TTL'd to under 48 hours and are trimmed during the decommission process. We will run a sweep to ensure no long-term indices are left behind.

- Routing behavior during migration: If BrightEdge goes away and traffic needs to be handled while the new provider is onboarded, our smart routing will prefer same-region Redwood pools when capacity exists. If we need to route to the US (temporary failover), requests will be handled by the Redwood-hosted US pool under the same SCCs/SCC-based safeguards we already rely on, but note: UK IDTA/UK addendum alignment requires an explicit on-record acknowledgment for temporary cross-border fallback.

- Contractual ask: From a product/ops standpoint, a short DPA exhibit that documents the decommission timeline and temporary fallback routing (with defined rollback windows) is sufficient. If legal wants a time-limited routing exception signed, we can provide a 1-page exhibit and a DocuSign route.

Action items:
1) Kimberly: confirm whether we want to provide the 1-page exhibit or simply an email statement (legal preference).
2) Naomi: can you confirm whether the existing SCCs + IDTA already in the customer's DPA cover temporary cross-border fallback, or whether the UK addendum requires separate sign-off?
3) Ops: I'll run a decommission sweep and provide a short verification note when complete (ETA: Oct 27).

David

Hi Marta — thanks for the heads up and the transfer log. A few clarifications and the customer's next steps below.

Clarifications:
- Legal coverage: Your existing DPA references the standard EU SCCs we execute with enterprise customers and includes the UK Addendum by virtue of the signed UK IDTA that was exchanged at contracting. That means temporary routing to the US is contractually permissible for fallbacks, but the UK addendum requires that the customer be notified and the temporary routing be limited to the narrowest necessary scope.

- Suggested evidence and ask: To avoid a formal addendum signature, many customers accept a short routing exhibit (1 page) plus a dated email confirmation acknowledging both (a) the timeline and (b) the limited purpose (failover/onboarding). If you prefer a signature, we can route a DocuSign 1-page exhibit.

Proposed text for a one-paragraph customer confirmation you can send to your legal ops: 
"CardioWorks acknowledges that during the BrightEdge Analytics decommission window (target week of Oct 25–29, 2026) Redwood Inference may temporarily route certain EU-origin requests to Redwood-hosted US pools for operational continuity. Such fallback routing will be limited to requests for which same-region capacity is not available, will be used only for the duration of the onboarding window, and will not result in long-term retention of CardioWorks session tokens; transient artifacts will be deleted as part of the decommission sweep."

If that language is acceptable, reply with either (A) an email confirmation against that paragraph or (B) say you want the DocuSign exhibit and we’ll send the link.

I will include a brief verification note once Ops completes its sweep (David noted ETA Oct 27).

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
Redwood Inference
